statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON (green). Tail is low at 11% while Stress is extreme at 81%.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the 25% block threshold, so the deterministic mapping resolves to EA_ON. NQ futures have drifted to a new overnight low at 29,364.00 and trade at 29,382.50, down 0.22%, but the whole overnight band spans only about 0.39% and the DOJ antitrust report on Nvidia's Groq licensing deal is being absorbed without dislocation. The extreme Stress reading describes the regime rather than the observed index path: long-end Treasury yields sit near 52-week highs and Brent is above $101 on the unresolved Strait of Hormuz disruption. August PPI, core PPI and initial jobless claims print at 12:30 UTC. A narrow elevated-risk window is flagged from 12:25 to 14:15 UTC spanning that release and the US cash open; outside it, conditions are described as orderly.
headline: NQ futures ease 0.22% to a new overnight low at 29,364.00 in a 0.39% band as the Nvidia antitrust report is absorbed, with Brent above $101 and long-end yields near 52-week highs
body:
The Nasdaq-100 closed the 9 September session at 29,421.55, down 0.29%, inside a 29,334.40-29,563.60 range of about 0.78%. In the current overnight hour, NQ futures trade at 29,382.50, down 0.22%, in a 29,364.00-29,480.25 band of roughly 0.39%. Price sits near the lower edge of that band and has just printed a fresh overnight low, extending the mild downward drift that began after a New York Times report, carried by Reuters, that the Justice Department is examining whether Nvidia's Groq licensing deal was structured to avoid antitrust premerger review. That is a genuine directional tilt and price is holding near a session extreme, which is why Tail is set one point above the prior hour at 11%. It is not yet trend evidence: the entire overnight range is under 0.4%, there is no observed sequence of failed retracements, and the repricing has proceeded in small increments in thin Asian liquidity.

The stress channels remain external to the index path. Treasury par yields rose again on 9 September to 4.17% at 2 years, 4.83% at 10 years and 5.28% at 30 years, with the long end near 52-week highs after the Treasury said it would triple its longer-dated buyback operation. Crude is firm but no longer extending: WTI trades at $96.53, up 0.50%, and Brent at $101.31, up 0.10%, marginally below the levels recorded an hour earlier while the Strait of Hormuz disruption stays unresolved and tanker transit counts remain far below the pre-crisis baseline. VIX finished the cash session at 16.46, up 4.71%, still low in absolute terms. Shared delayed cross-asset context was collected more than 90 minutes before this assessment and showed index futures marginally higher; it is stale under the applied freshness rule, is contradicted by the fresher live quote, and is therefore not used as price-path evidence here.

The next scheduled catalysts are August PPI, core PPI and initial jobless claims at 12:30 UTC, followed by August existing home sales at 14:00 UTC, August CPI on 11 September, and the two-day FOMC meeting on 15-16 September with a Summary of Economic Projections. Those are checkpoints rather than observed structure: before a print, event importance and forecast dispersion inform Stress and Confidence rather than Tail. Confidence of 87% reflects verified current futures, cash-close, volatility, yield, crude, geopolitical and calendar evidence, reduced by one point because the shared cross-asset context is stale for this hour.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the preceding 24 clock-hours carry a published Claude assessment; the 10:00-11:00 UTC slot on 9 September has none and is marked unavailable. Tail ran between 7% and 9% through the Asian and European overnight, peaked at 20% in the 12:00 UTC hour, the single yellow WATCH slot in the window, then decayed through the US cash session and held at 8-10% from 21:00 UTC onward as price discovery stayed orderly. Stress climbed from 74% to an 83% peak and settled near 80-81%, driven by rates and crude rather than index path damage. Confidence held in an 87-89% band throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail in a 10-12% band through the Asian and European overnight, where the dominant mechanisms are continued absorption of the Nvidia antitrust report and headline discontinuity from the Strait of Hormuz into thin liquidity, rather than trend persistence. Tail then steps up into the 12:30 UTC PPI, core PPI and claims block and peaks at 20%, mapping to WATCH, in the 13:00 UTC hour where post-release repricing overlaps the US cash open. It decays back toward the overnight baseline through the US afternoon, with a small lift into the power hour before the 20:00 UTC close, then a flat overnight path that edges up in the final slot as pre-CPI sensitivity builds. Stress stays extreme throughout, peaking at 87% in the cash-open hour, and Confidence declines from 87% to 76% as each slot moves further from verified live evidence.
